definition: The process of using a trained model to generate predictions or outputs on new input data, as opposed to training the model.
details: Inference is where most of an LLM's real-world compute cost accumulates over time (since a model may be trained once but run millions of times), driving significant engineering effort toward inference optimization.
story: Imagine a sketch artist who starts with static and, stroke by stroke, sharpens it into a face. The result feels creative because it is memory, reshuffled at speed. Given a starting line, the machine imagines what comes next — a word, a note, a patch of a picture. The model dreams a little, then cleans up the dream. That next-word, next-stroke magic is Inference.
